scope: Proposition 3.5 (Cluster and transmission counts) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following bounds hold in fixed buffered boxes, uniformly in the mesh and in allowed conditional histories. A joint count of actual clusters across chambers in items 1 and 3 requires the product class with a common fill. Item 2 has the interior scope stated there. 1. For fixed b > 0, the number of unsearched free N clusters having a connected passage of diameter at least b in a fixed box has an exponential tail. Its constants depend on b and the fixed box geometry, not on the roughness of the surrounding walls or on the number of chambers in the realization with a common fill. 2. For one chamber, let a lattice-aligned rectangle and its joining buffer lie wholly in the unprescribed accessible interior. Use the relative dual restriction with separate side ports defined in the proof. The number of distinct components of the restricted N graph crossing between two specified opposite sides has a geometric tail. Consequently, if Q0 ⋐ Q1, the number of restricted components in Q1 which meet Q0 and a vertex incident to an edge outside the restriction has a geometric tail, provided the fixed covering rectangles in Q1 \ Q0 and every joining buffer have the same unprescribed interior clearance. Arbitrary admissible (s, W) prescriptions outside a larger buffer are allowed. The same interior assertion holds in the original wired law before removal of its boundary cluster. 3. Counts of distinct free N clusters of the residual kernels enclosing or passing through a fixed aspect-ratio annular shell have moments of every fixed order, uniformly after rescaling the shell down to lattice order. Under a stopping history these are the unsearched clusters. A distinguished wired cluster adds at most one. For arbitrary independent chambers with pairwise disjoint interiors this last statement is available separately in each chamber; it asserts no bound for their total count without a common fill. The precise no-shadowing consequence at indexed discoveries is stated in Theorem 3.8 below.
